title: Metric card
description: Formalization of a benchmark performance metric. Language-neutral; readable from Python (jsonschema) and R (jsonvalidate). Schema version 1.2: comparability gains the optional noise_floor scalar (smallest interpretable difference in native units), consumed by beam.mcda.noise_floor_separation. Schema version 1.1 added the typed mappings block (stato, uo, obi, qudt, om2, huggingface_evaluate); additionalProperties stays true so a card can carry private or future keys without a schema bump.

version.description: Card version, e.g. v1 or v1.2.

metric_kind.description: derived: computed from inputs (e.g. ARI from two label vectors). measured: observed during execution (e.g. runtime, peak memory).

target.description: Ideal value of a target_value metric, in native units (calibration slope: 1). Consumed by the target_relative normalization, which scales each method by its closeness to this value.

score_of_random_baseline.description: Value a chance-level method reaches on this metric, in native units. ARI: 0 (corrected for chance). Consumed by the baseline_relative normalization so a method no better than chance maps to 0 instead of the column midpoint.

recommended_aggregation_across_datasets.description: Machine-readable hint for how to reduce per-dataset scores of this metric to a per-tool summary. Smith 1988: ratio metrics with values spanning orders of magnitude (runtime, peak memory) take geometric mean; bounded interval or ratio metrics take arithmetic mean unless an outlier-robust summary is wanted.

recommended_normalization.description: Machine-readable hint for how the MCDA pipeline should rescale this metric to [0, 1] before weighting. min_max for bounded metrics; log_min_max for ratio metrics spanning orders of magnitude (runtime, peak memory) so a single outlier does not compress the rest (Smith 1988); rank for a scale-free outlier-proof rescale; zscore for a logistic-squashed standardization; baseline_relative for chance-corrected metrics so a chance-level method maps to 0 rather than the column midpoint; target_relative for target_value metrics, scaling each method by its closeness to the declared semantics.target so the method nearest the target maps to 1.

noise_floor.description: Smallest difference in native units that is interpretable on this metric; differences below it are measurement noise. Consumed by beam.mcda.noise_floor_separation to flag tool pairs the metric set cannot tell apart, so the report does not present an order that rests on a sub-noise-floor difference. Source per metric: a reproducibility study or a Gauge R&R measurement.

mappings.description: Cross-references to external ontologies and metric registries. Known keys are typed below; the block stays open so cards may carry future keys without a schema bump. Values are full IRIs (preferred) or stable URLs. The known keys are: stato (Statistics Ontology, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/STATO_NNNNNNN), uo (Units of Measurement Ontology, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UO_NNNNNNN), obi (Ontology for Biomedical Investigations, http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_NNNNNNN), qudt (QUDT units), om2 (Ontology of Units of Measure version 2), and huggingface_evaluate (URL of the HuggingFace evaluate metric card directory).
